To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

superporous hydrogel interpenetrating networks were synthesized by radical copolymerization in the presence gas blowing agent, and they have a structure of interconnect pores and can load protein by solvent sorption very rapidly with high capacities and release the protein very fast.
superporous hydrogel (SPH) and superporous hydro-gel interpenetrating network (SPH-IPN) are developed as a novel protein delivery system.
superporous polyacrylic acid/chitosan interpenetrating network hydrogels were successfully synthesized and characterized and that these hydrogels were used as protein delivery systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new superporous poly(AAm) and poly(AAm) with AA hydrogels and their interpenetrating poly(AAm)-chitosan and poly(AAm-AA)-chitosan hydrogels for the delivery of protein.
the synthesis and characterization of superporous hydrogel interpenetrating networks (SPH-IPNs) with high porosities and high pore sizes for protein delivery.
the synthesis of superporous polyacrylic acid hydrogels and their interpenetrating network hydrogels with chitosan.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
superporous hydrogel structure can be used as a promising carrier for protein delivery applications.
SPHs and especially SPH-IPN hydrogels can be successfully applied as protein delivery systems.
the SPH-IPN hydrogels are a promising candidate for protein delivery systems with a very high loading and release capacities in a short period of time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SPHs have very fast equilibrium swelling and very high protein loading capacities and the SPH-IPN hydrogels have very fast protein delivery rates.
superporous hydrogel networks are suitable materials for protein delivery applications.
the superporous hydrogel technology can be applied to develop novel protein delivery systems with very high loading capacities and fast release profiles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
superporous hydrogel networks can be used to prepare superporous IPNs for controlled protein delivery.
the developed SPHs and IPN hydrog gels are suitable for protein delivery and can be used as drug carriers for oral drug delivery.
SPH-IPN hydrogels can be used as an efficient carrier system for the delivery of proteins in a very short time.
